## Purpose

This SOP describes the laboratory procedures for sorting, subsampling,
and identifying benthic macroinvertebrates (BMI) collected from wadeable
streams per [SOP-F610](../field_sops/SOP-F610-macroinvertebrate-sampling.qmd).
The procedure follows the California Surface Water Ambient Monitoring
Program (SWAMP) laboratory processing protocols to ensure compatibility
with statewide bioassessment datasets [@ode2016; @barbour1999].
Taxonomic identifications are used to calculate biological condition
metrics, including the California Stream Condition Index (CSCI)
[@mazor2016].


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Laboratory processing of ethanol-preserved BMI
  samples from wadeable streams, including subsampling, sorting,
  identification to the lowest practical taxonomic level, and
  enumeration
- **Does not apply to:** Field collection of BMI (see
  [SOP-F610](../field_sops/SOP-F610-macroinvertebrate-sampling.qmd));
  marine or estuarine macroinvertebrates; meiofauna (organisms passing
  through a 500 $\mu$m sieve); molecular identification (eDNA
  metabarcoding)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                                          |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------------------|
| PI / Lab Manager  | Approve taxonomic level targets; arrange external QC    |
| Trained Personnel | Sort, identify, and enumerate organisms per this SOP    |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent sorting            |

## Definitions

- **Benthic macroinvertebrate (BMI):** An invertebrate organism inhabiting the bottom substrate of streams, lakes, or wetlands that is retained on a 500 µm mesh sieve; includes aquatic insects, crustaceans, worms, mollusks, and other taxa.
- **Fixed count subsample:** A randomly selected subset of a BMI sample from which a fixed number of organisms (e.g., 500) is picked and identified; reduces processing time for large samples while maintaining statistical reliability.
- **Functional feeding group (FFG):** A classification of macroinvertebrates by feeding mode (shredders, collectors-gatherers, collectors-filterers, scrapers/grazers, predators); used to assess stream ecosystem function from invertebrate assemblage data.
- **Qualitative identification:** Determination of taxa present in a sample without quantifying abundances; used for rapid bioassessment and presence/absence monitoring.
- **Quantitative sample:** A sample in which all organisms are counted and identified to calculate density (organisms per unit area or volume); requires accurate recording of sampled area and volume.
- **Taxonomic resolution:** The level of taxonomic identification applied to BMI specimens; options range from phylum/class to order, family, genus, or species; standard SWAMP protocol requires family-level identification for most groups.
- **Voucher specimen:** A representative specimen of a taxon retained in preservative as a reference for future verification; essential for quality assurance and resolving taxonomic uncertainties.


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Preserved samples contain approximately 70% ethanol,
  which is flammable and an inhalation irritant. Work in a
  well-ventilated area away from ignition sources.
- **Physical:** Forceps and dissecting needles are sharp. Use caution
  when handling small organisms.
- **Biological:** Stream organisms may harbor parasites or pathogens.
  Wear gloves when handling preserved samples.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat

### Emergency Procedures

For ethanol spills, ventilate the area, absorb with paper towels, and
dispose in flammable waste. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Notes                                    |
|:--------------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Dissecting microscope (stereo)        | 7--45x magnification; illuminated base   |
| Compound microscope                   | For slide-mounted specimens requiring higher magnification |
| Gridded Caton sorting tray            | White, subdivided into numbered cells    |
| Fine-tipped forceps (2 pairs)         | Dumont #5 or equivalent                  |
| Dissecting needles                    | For separating tangled organisms         |
| Petri dishes                          | For isolating specimens during ID        |
| Wash bottles (ethanol and DI water)   |                                          |

### Consumables

| Item                              | Notes                              |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------|
| 70% ethanol                       | For topping off vials              |
| Scintillation vials (20 mL)       | For archiving sorted taxa          |
| Labels (pencil on waterproof paper) | Internal and external labels     |
| Depression slides                 | For compound microscope work       |


## Procedure

### Sample Receiving and Logging

1. Verify that the sample jar label matches the chain-of-custody or
   field data sheet: site ID, date, collector, preservative.
2. Log the sample into the laboratory tracking spreadsheet.
3. Inspect the sample for adequate preservative (organisms should not
   appear soft or discolored). If the ethanol is diluted below
   approximately 50%, decant carefully and replace with fresh 70%
   ethanol before proceeding.

### Subsampling

The SWAMP standard requires identification of a minimum of 500
organisms per sample. A fixed-count random subsampling procedure is
used [@caton1991]:

1. Pour the entire sample through a 500 $\mu$m sieve. Rinse the jar
   into the sieve to recover all material.
2. Transfer the sieved material to the gridded Caton sorting tray.
   Distribute the material as evenly as possible across all grid cells.
3. Use a random number generator or random number table to select grid
   cells for sorting.
4. Under the dissecting microscope, remove all organisms from the
   selected cell using forceps, transferring them to a labeled petri
   dish or vial. Count each organism as it is picked.
5. Continue selecting and sorting random cells until the cumulative
   organism count reaches or exceeds 500. Complete the cell in
   progress even if the count exceeds 500 mid-cell.
6. Record the number of cells sorted, the total cells in the tray,
   and the total organism count.

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Keep the residue (unsorted cells) in a labeled jar with 70% ethanol.
The residue is needed for the re-sort QC check and may be required if
additional identifications are needed later.
:::

### Identification

1. Separate sorted organisms into major taxonomic groups (e.g.,
   Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, Trichoptera, Diptera, Coleoptera,
   non-insect taxa) under the dissecting microscope.
2. Identify each organism to the lowest practical taxonomic level
   using standard keys [@merritt2019; @thorp2015]:
   - Insects: genus (family for early instars or damaged specimens)
   - Non-insect invertebrates: family or order (depending on group
     and specimen condition)
3. For specimens requiring higher magnification (e.g., chironomid
   head capsules, oligochaete chaetae), prepare slide mounts and
   examine under the compound microscope.
4. Record counts by taxon on the laboratory data sheet or directly
   into the data entry spreadsheet.

### Voucher Specimens

1. Retain at least one representative specimen of each taxon as a
   voucher in a labeled scintillation vial with 70% ethanol.
2. Label each vial with: site ID, date, taxon name, identifier
   initials, identification date.
3. Store voucher vials in the BMI reference collection.

### Data Entry and Metric Calculation

1. Enter identification data into the standardized spreadsheet or
   database.
2. Calculate summary metrics:
   - Total taxa richness
   - EPT (Ephemeroptera, Plecoptera, Trichoptera) richness
   - Percent tolerant taxa
   - Percent dominant taxon
   - Shannon diversity index ($H'$)
3. If sufficient data are available, calculate the CSCI score using
   the CSCI R package or the online CSCI calculator [@mazor2016].


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
# Example: Shannon diversity from BMI count data
library(vegan)

# counts is a named vector of organism counts by taxon
counts <- c(Baetis = 120, Hydropsyche = 85, Chironomidae = 210,
            Simulium = 45, Optioservus = 30, Physa = 10)

H_prime <- diversity(counts, index = "shannon")
cat(sprintf("Shannon H': %.3f\n", H_prime))
cat(sprintf("Total taxa: %d\n", length(counts)))
cat(sprintf("Total organisms: %d\n", sum(counts)))
cat(sprintf("EPT richness: count EPT genera from full dataset\n"))
```
:::



## Quality Control

- **Sorting efficiency:** Re-sort 10% of processed samples (randomly
  selected). The re-sort technician examines all residue material from
  the original subsampling. Sorting efficiency must be greater than or
  equal to 90% (i.e., fewer than 10% of total organisms were missed).
- **Taxonomic verification:** Have a second identifier verify
  identifications for 10% of specimens. Agreement should be greater
  than or equal to 90% at the operational taxonomic level.
- **External QC:** For data submitted to SWAMP or CEDEN, submit 10%
  of samples to a SWAMP-certified taxonomic laboratory for independent
  re-identification.
- Record all QC results in the QC log.


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Ethanol from samples          | Evaporate in fume hood or collect in flammable waste |
| Sorted residue (organic material) | Drain ethanol; dispose in standard trash |
| Used gloves and paper towels  | Standard trash                           |

## Training Record

Before sorting and identifying BMI independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP and
   [SOP-F610](../field_sops/SOP-F610-macroinvertebrate-sampling.qmd) in
   full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the major taxonomic keys [@merritt2019; @thorp2015]
4. Complete a supervised sorting exercise achieving greater than 90%
   sorting efficiency
5. Correctly identify a training set of at least 30 taxa under
   supervision (greater than 85% agreement with reference
   identifications)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
